name: Shunning
overview: Scripture instructs believers to exercise careful discernment in relationships, balancing correction with grace. While we are commanded to avoid those who cause divisions and oppose sound doctrine, as Paul urges in Romans 16:17, we are also reminded not to judge hastily or seek personal vengeance (Matthew 7:1; Romans 12:19). Jesus’ teaching in Matthew 18:15 emphasizes private confrontation to restore a brother who has sinned, while His welcoming of sinners in Luke 15:1 and Peter’s revelation in Acts 10:28 show that God calls His people to avoid labeling others as unclean or common. Thus, shunning in the biblical sense is a measured response aimed at protecting the church’s purity without forsaking the call to love and restoration.
